In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a positive cosmic acceleration is possible in spatially averaged Lemaître-Tolman-Bondi cosmologies, but only under the following conditions: the 3-curvature must be positive; the spatial average must be taken over a large enough domain of space; the spatial average of the matter density must be low; the expansion must be fast; and, the expansion must have started from a very high initial density.

the spatial averaging of the matter density is not sufficient to cause the acceleration of the Universe, but it is possible to find models where spatial averaging of matter density can cause the acceleration.

the possibility of cosmic acceleration is not ruled out by spatial averaging in a Lemaître?Tolman-Bondi cosmology, although there are strong reasons to believe that this is a very unlikely possibility, if not impossible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a positive acceleration in a spatial averaging scenario can only occur for models with a large 3-curvature, and that this is only possible in the limit of a vanishing average matter density.
the acceleration can be obtained only in the case of a very low matter density, but in this case, it would be very short lived, and the universe would eventually collapse.

, in a spatially flat, homogeneous, expanding cosmology, a positive cosmic acceleration can be obtained if and only if the universe is spatially closed and the spatial average of the 3-curvature scalar is negative.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the acceleration is not due to the presence of dark energy, but to the spatial averaging of the matter distribution in a non-uniform, inhomogeneous, and unbound universe.
the possibility of acceleration in a homogeneous, unbound LTB universe cannot be ruled out on theoretical grounds.
the acceleration is not a generic feature of these models.
